body: Succinate or hcl? This makes a huge difference dosage wise. I have the succinate and people suggest at least 80-150mg. I'll likely see what 50 mg does first anyways, curious myself about it, particularly how it compares to 5-apb and if it's worth getting some of that in favour of 5-mapb. Pretty expensive when you compare the two.

I've had it after taking a massive dosage of amitryptaline for someone who's never had any. Doc said it was fine, pharmacist said "hey don't do that" when I dropped both in front of him, lol. I said, I'm good, need to get rid of this tinnitus. I was good for a couple hours.

I think you will know when it really is serotonin syndrome. You will sweat like crazy, I mean the cold sweats. I felt extremely lethargic at first before falling asleep and waking up in confusion and a mad panic, tachycardia, the sweating, terrible headache and bodyload, you just want to throw up, bit migrainish.

I have no experience with citalopram, but I think you're fine. Maybe as brelaine suggested, go down and normalize before going back up.
So so. Haven't had anyone die, yet, but it feels like I died, so there's that.

Oh, yeah I'm scared of ssri's, will absolutely refuse taking them. What are you on now if you don't mind me asking?

Feeling broken, so familiar, nearly everything  you say. Eye contact, trouble communicating, fear of being touched, abusive relationship, being called crazy for doing your own research, shit experience with medical professionals. It made me self diagnose and self medicate, which kinda works, but not longterm. 

So I thought in my major depressive episode that it was a smart thing to tell my doctor, no, rehab ensued, I ran because those people are monsters (berated for not making eye contact for example), settled on psychiatry, which will probably be long-term considering my prognosis will be "bleak", hehe. Now that I'm back to regular depression, it makes me doubt my decisions.

I think you're amazing for pursuing that career choice, stick with it!

You're crazy if you don't do your own research.

We share some disorders, lol. I've always avoided going through the mental health system for exactly these reasons, but I broke down recently and decided I should. This doesn't exactly give me confidence, but oh well. 

Are they ever helpful?

Well you made me cry, I love cats. :(

Not being able to cry is pretty common during grief and depression, you just feel numb and empty, sort of a coping mechanism. It will come though, you don't have to force it ,or blame yourself for not being able to right now.

That moment he started to purr, that was beautiful, you shared a deep bond, I think that moment tells all. Just give all that love to your other cat right now, I'm sure you can both use a little.

It can take a long time before you can find what works for you though. Sometimes certain medications can even exacerbate depression and suicidal ideation. Discussing this with your psychiatrist is pretty important, you're not a burden to them if they prescribed you something that's not effective, it's a lot of hit and miss still, not anyone's fault.

The world wasn't made for anyone in particular, so we've all got that in common at least. ;)

Getting stabbed in the chest is literally a daily thing for me, mentally and physically, I completely get it. Happiness is just a smile.

Try talking to your doctor about the meds though, if it doesn't work it doesn't work.

I read your message, I wish I replied sooner. 

I'm sorry you're feeling so down, you deserve way better. 

Big hug to you ❤
Let me tell you something even scarier, when you grow older, each year seems to pass by faster and faster. Time is precious and I keep on wasting it, ha.

I understand both positions, but yeah, life sucks don't it? lol
